questions.text: A certain processor uses a fully associative cache of size 16 kB, The cache block size is 16 bytes. Assume that the main memory is byte addressable and uses a 32-bit address. How many bits are required for the Tag and the Index fields respectively in the addresses generated by the processor?
questions.solution:
Fully associative cache has no index field (a block can go in any line).

Block size 16 bytes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] offset = 4 bits. Tag = 32 [latex]-[/latex] 4 = 28 bits.

Answer: 28 bits and 0 bits

questions.text: The chip select logic for a certain DRAM chip in a memory system design is shown below. Assume that the memory system has 16 address lines denoted by [latex]A_{15} \; to \; A_0[/latex]. What is the range of address (in hexadecimal) of the memory system that can get enabled by the chip select (CS) signal?
questions.solution:
CS = 1 only when [latex]A_{15}=1,\ A_{14}=1,\ A_{13}=0,\ A_{12}=0,\ A_{11}=1[/latex] (A13 and A12 enter through inverting bubbles). A10-A0 can be anything.

- Lowest: 1100 1000 0000 0000 = C800
- Highest: 1100 1111 1111 1111 = CFFF

Answer: C800 to CFFF

questions.text: Which one of the following kinds of derivation is used by LR parsers?
questions.solution:
An LR parser works bottom-up: it repeatedly reduces handles. The sequence of reductions is exactly a rightmost derivation traced in reverse.

Answer: Rightmost in reverse

questions.text: In 16-bit 2's complement representation, the decimal number -28 is:
questions.solution:
+28 in 16 bits = 0000 0000 0001 1100.
2's complement: invert [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1111 1111 1110 0011, add 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1111 1111 1110 0100.

Answer: 1111 1111 1110 0100

questions.text:
Let [latex]U=\{1,2,,...n\}[/latex]. Let [latex]A=\{(x,X)|x\in X,X\subseteq U\}[/latex]. Consider the following two statements on |A|.

I. [latex]|A|=n2^{n-1}[/latex]
II. [latex]|A|=\sum_{k=1}^{n}k\binom{n}{k}[/latex]

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Count the pairs (x, X) with [latex]x\in X[/latex] in two ways:
- Fix x first: x lies in [latex]2^{n-1}[/latex] subsets, so [latex]|A|=n\,2^{n-1}[/latex].
- Fix the size k of X first: there are [latex]\binom nk[/latex] such sets, each giving k choices of x, so [latex]|A|=\sum_{k=1}^{n}k\binom nk[/latex].

Both are correct (and equal).

Answer: Both I and II
